But it departs from the B+ tree in three ways suited to LLM access: content lives at every level, the pages are plain text rather than attribute values, and navigation follows the relevance of a page summary to the question rather than a key comparison. The structure itself is discovered per document by the LLM rather than hand-designed in advance. In a preliminary evaluation on narrative and contract corpora, Periplus comes within 0.1--0.9 percentage points of the strongest baseline's accuracy while consuming 70--72\% fewer total tokens. These early results are encouraging, and they offer only a glimpse of what index design can bring to LLM-based analysis.
papers.summary: Position paper: reuse database index design for LLM document analysis; Periplus is a B+-tree-like hierarchy of plain-text summaries navigated by relevance, using 70% fewer tokens.

papers.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
papers.curator_blurb: Tests why search agents keep an earlier wrong answer (missing the source, not reading the passage, or not revising and finishing the answer).
papers.summary: Diagnoses why search agents keep wrong earlier answers: missing the source, not reading the passage, or not revising.

papers.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Web-scale recommender models evolve primarily through retraining or fine-tuning. We propose \emph{weight coding}, a methodology for model evolution through direct, executable weight edits. A large language model (LLM) agent inspects model structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and implements edits using evaluation feedback. The loop progresses from localized changes to targeted searches and composition, allowing edited components to adapt to one another. A cached engine enables rapid forward evaluation without backpropagation. On Pinterest's 147M-parameter Image Search two-tower retriever, weight coding improves held-out recall@10 of production model by up to 15.0 percentage points (+24\% relative) with few edits in about 1/4 GPU hours of a full post-training finetune, while a common launch only improves around 1\%. After reinitializing the entire 13.6M-parameter interaction module randomly while retaining the surrounding trained model, searching 2,448 mixing and normalization parameters yields 9.8 points above production. Offline gains span the full funnel including dense retrieval, generative retrieval and ranking, with up to 1.37B learnable parameters and different edits for each architecture. Steering edits provide explicit control of model performance over segments like freshness and product. Weight coding requires no serving change and online A/B tests increase saves per user from the edited retrieval source by 8.4\% to 10.7\%, aligned with the target business objectives. Our results establish weight coding as a practical and useful tool for model development and and behavioral control in a real web-scale production system, with potential to extend to both pre-training and post-training stages across the funnel.
papers.curator_blurb: Pinterest presents weight coding, where an LLM agent improves a production recommender by editing its weights instead of retraining, with no serving changes.
papers.summary: Pinterest improves a production recommender by having an LLM agent edit its weights directly instead of retraining.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Agentic Era: Tradition, Present, and Prospect
papers.curator_blurb: Surveys RAG across its full lifecycle, from indexing to orchestration, treats agentic workflows as a paradigm of their own, and also covers evaluation.
papers.summary: Survey of RAG from indexing to orchestration, treating agentic workflows as their own paradigm.

papers.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents
papers.curator_blurb: Shows that memory-writing and retrieval policies distilled separately into 3B models can be combined without joint training and outperform RL-trained compositions.
papers.summary: Memory-writing and retrieval policies distilled separately into 3B models compose without joint training and beat RL-trained compositions.

papers.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
papers.curator_blurb: Introduces a method to split RL gains in search agents across reasoning, search decisions, query generation, and answer extraction via Shapley values.
papers.summary: Attributes RL gains in search agents to reasoning, search decisions, query generation and answer extraction via Shapley values over grafted policy roles.
